questions.stem: Mrs Costa, 29, is at 39+4 weeks on an oxytocin induction. Her membranes were ruptured artificially 20 minutes ago, with the head high at station -2. The fetal heart has dropped to 70 bpm for 3 minutes, and Sam confirms it is separate from the maternal pulse. You have explained what you are doing and she agrees. Which examination is the priority now?
options: Abdominal palpation to estimate how many fifths of the head are palpable
Digital vaginal examination to feel for the umbilical cord
Sterile speculum examination to look at the liquor and for bleeding
Palpation of the uterus between contractions for tenderness
questions.why: A sudden prolonged deceleration soon after ARM with a high head needs a vaginal examination to exclude cord prolapse. It is the only one of these steps that finds the cause and lets you treat it straight away by lifting the presenting part.
notes: The head level is already known (station -2). Counting fifths does not exclude cord prolapse or change what you do next.
A speculum is slower and does not let you elevate the presenting part. A digital examination both finds a prolapsed cord and treats it.
Checking for tenderness is reasonable for abruption, but she has no pain or bleeding. With a recent ARM and a high head, cord prolapse must be excluded first.

questions.stem: At 11:48 the cord is still pulsating below the presenting part and the fetal heart is about 90 bpm with reduced variability. The cervix is 5 cm, station -2. You are holding the presenting part up, the oxytocin is off and she is knee-chest. What plan for birth should the obstetric team make?
options: Fetal scalp blood sampling for lactate to decide how urgently to deliver
Category 2 caesarean, aiming for birth within about 75 minutes
Category 1 caesarean, aiming for birth as fast as is safely possible
Fill the bladder and continue labour towards an assisted vaginal birth
questions.why: Cord prolapse with a persistent bradycardia before full dilatation is an immediate threat to the fetus's life. It needs a category 1 caesarean, aiming for birth as fast as is safely possible (generally within 30 minutes), while the presenting part stays elevated until birth.
notes: Fetal blood sampling only delays birth. A prolonged deceleration or bradycardia that does not recover needs birth expedited, not sampling.
Category 2 is for compromise that is not an immediate threat to life. A pulsating, compressed cord with bradycardia is an immediate threat, so this is category 1.
Filling the bladder is only for when birth will be delayed, such as during transfer. Vaginal birth is an option only at full dilatation, and she is 5 cm.

questions.stem: Mrs Costa's BP was 110/65 before an epidural top-up. Fifteen minutes later, lying semi-recumbent, it is 84/50 with a maternal pulse of 105 to 108. She is alert and afebrile, with no bleeding. What is the main mechanism of her fall in blood pressure?
options: Sympathetic block causing vasodilation, venous pooling and reduced preload
Systemic local anaesthetic absorption directly depressing the myocardium
Block of the cardiac accelerator fibres (T1 to T4) causing primary bradycardia
Histamine release from the local anaesthetic causing anaphylactoid vasodilation
questions.why: Neuraxial local anaesthetic blocks sympathetic vasomotor outflow, causing arterial and venous dilation. Venous return falls, made worse by aortocaval compression. Uteroplacental flow has no autoregulation, so it falls with her BP. The tachycardia is the baroreflex response.
notes: Myocardial depression is a sign of local anaesthetic toxicity, which comes with neurological symptoms. She is alert, and a standard top-up does not cause this.
A high block reaching T1 to T4 would cause bradycardia. She is tachycardic, which shows her cardiac sympathetic drive and baroreflex are intact.
Amide local anaesthetics rarely release histamine. She has no rash, wheeze or other features of anaphylaxis.

questions.stem: After ARM, Sam's vaginal examination found Mrs Costa 5 cm dilated, vertex LOA, 3/5 of the head palpable abdominally and station -2. Twenty minutes later a cord prolapse is found. What does station -2 describe?
options: The leading part of the vertex is 2 cm below the level of the ischial spines
Two-fifths of the fetal head remain palpable above the pelvic brim
The leading part of the vertex is 2 cm above the plane of the pelvic inlet
The leading bony part of the fetal skull is 2 cm above the ischial spines
questions.why: Station is the level of the leading bony part of the fetal skull relative to the ischial spines: negative above, positive below. At -2 the head is high and not engaged, which leaves room for the cord to slip past after ARM.
notes: Below the spines is a positive station (+2). A head that low would be well engaged and unlikely to allow a cord prolapse.
Fifths palpable is an abdominal measure of descent, and she is 3/5 palpable. It is not the same as station on vaginal examination.
Station is measured from the ischial spines, not the pelvic inlet. The inlet is a higher plane at the brim of the pelvis.
